dataMgmt.readonlyNotice: This page covers overview / trend / data health / cleanup preview and execution / TTL and retention policy. Cleanup and TTL are actions: they require double confirmation and a passing pre-cleanup reconciliation, and they write an audit entry plus a cleaned-range registration. Future-timestamp junk (devices with skewed clocks) is detected and reported only — never deleted automatically.

guide.title: What is this page for?
guide.whatBody: This is a side-path integrity check: it reconciles sa_events (written by our ingestor) against log_analysis (written by the community Flink job) day by day, to catch stalled consumption, silent data loss and duplicate writes. It is read-only and never touches business data; by default it checks yesterday automatically once a day at the off-peak time (03:30 platform timezone) and stores the result as a snapshot.

terms.range: Range: yesterday by default; up to 3 days manually (a single-node memory guard set after past OOM incidents).
terms.threshold: Threshold: a day is flagged only when |deviation| exceeds it; see the config row above (percent).
terms.crc: CRC uniqueness: approximate dedup within our side only; flagged when duplicate rows exceed 0.5% (the approximate algorithm has inherent error).
terms.trusted: Trusted range: comparable only within the shorter of the two retention windows; dates beyond it are marked "beyond retention" and excluded from anomalies.
terms.skipped: Cleaned ranges: periods removed on purpose via DROP PARTITION / TTL are marked "cleaned" and excluded from alerting.
terms.stale: Snapshot freshness: when the snapshot is stale (yellow/red) the conclusion no longer reflects reality — re-run reconciliation or check the scheduler.
terms.events: Top event diffs: events present on both sides with different counts, top 20 by absolute diff; "only one side" lists events where the other side is 0.

how.step1: A sustained +1% to +2% daily deviation is a known structural caliber difference (the community side under-counts Android error/retry events — see the caliber whitepaper), not data loss.
how.step2: Investigate immediately when: the deviation turns negative (we have fewer than the community side), an event count drops to zero, or a new event type suddenly appears in the diffs.
how.step3: Days marked "beyond retention" or "cleaned" are not counted as anomalies; a failing CRC suggests duplicate writes on our side.
how.step4: The 3-day manual limit is a deliberate memory guard; for longer spans use the off-peak wide-range job (scripts/reconcile.sh --type=range on the server).

who.admin: Platform super admin: change threshold/ignore list/stale windows via "Reconcile settings" (top right), and handle failure or staleness notifications.
who.oncall: On-call: check "Top event diffs" first to tell a new event type from a whole event disappearing, then look at the daily totals trend on both sides.
who.analyst: Analysts: this page is not for business analysis; check pipeline health under Ops → Data management → Data health.

projectRetire.title: Project retirement preview
projectRetire.communityNote: Community tables (clklog.log_analysis and 18 aggregates) have no project dimension, so they cannot be cleaned per project; use retention/TTL to reduce them over time

step.stopWrites: Stop reporting for this project first (disable its API key / stop the SDK) and confirm writes in the last 24h drop to zero
step.execution: Run the retirement: delete per table on the sa side (DROP PARTITION for member tables, ALTER DELETE otherwise) plus table-by-table deletion in MySQL
step.backupAudit: Rows to delete are exported to a backup file first, and the action is audited (action=project_retire)
